title: The Evening Brief: Watson returns; FIFA's African split widens; Lakers sale clears $12.5B
dek: Deshaun Watson takes the field for the first time since October 2024 as the Browns' preseason opener arrives, while FIFA's governance crisis deepened with six Arab federations backing Infantino even as major continental confederations and national associations withdrew support. The Lakers' record $12.5 billion sale awaits NBA board approval in September.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: FIFA's coalition fractured into explicit opposition: UEFA, CONCACAF, AFC, and several national associations issued public condemnation of Infantino's withdrawn privatization plan, while Arab federations countered with public backing, setting the stage for a contested 2027 election with a November deadline for challengers.
bottom_line: The evening crystallized FIFA's governance fault lines with explicit continental opposition and counter-backing, while preseason quarterback debuts and injury updates set the calendar for the coming weekend. The reporting establishes the positions taken by major confederations and Arab federations but does not resolve vote trajectories ahead of any 2027 FIFA challenge. Watson's return, Pearsall's recovery timeline, and the Lakers' September board approval are the coming checkpoints.
body: The evening's dominant story is FIFA's governance crisis moving from backroom disputes into open continental division. Isha Johansen's morning call for Infantino to resign marked the first prominent African football figure to break with continental consensus, invoking Infantino's own 2021 advice to her to step down for the good of football. By Thursday afternoon, six Arab federations declared full support for him, but the larger structural damage was already visible: UEFA, CONCACAF, and AFC issued a joint letter condemning his withdrawn $20 billion World Cup privatization proposal as a "fundamental breach of trust," while England, Wales, and Ireland formally withdrew their support for his 2027 reelection. The reporting establishes the positions taken and the explicit grounds for opposition, but does not resolve whether organized confederations can field a credible challenger before the November 18 deadline for candidacy or whether Infantino's Arab and remaining African backing will hold through a March 2027 vote.

On the field, the preseason weekend arrived with several injury-driven storylines. Deshaun Watson is set to start Saturday's Browns opener against Chicago in his first live action since tearing his right Achilles tendon in October 2024 and undergoing a second surgery in January 2025. He missed the entire 2025 season. Shedeur Sanders will start the Browns' second preseason game on August 22, keeping the quarterback competition unresolved. In Buffalo, Josh Allen and all healthy starters will play Saturday against Carolina at the new Highmark Stadium, marking the Bills' first game in the venue and Allen's first preseason appearance since 2024. The 49ers placed Ricky Pearsall on season-ending injured reserve after he underwent posterior cruciate ligament repair surgery, targeting a nine-month recovery to return for the 2027 season. He appeared in only 20 games across three NFL seasons. Arizona's Carson Beck, the Cardinals' rookie quarterback, sat out Thursday's preseason game against Las Vegas as a precaution after sustaining a rib injury during the Hall of Fame Game; team sources told ESPN the injury carries "zero long-term worry." Philadelphia's Moro Ojomo and Fred Johnson fought during the final training-camp practice Thursday before the Eagles' preseason opener against Baltimore; both remained on the roster.

On transfers and signings, Inter Milan advanced negotiations with Tottenham for full-back Djed Spence in a deal valued at approximately 25.6 million pounds, with no agreement finalized as of the latest updates. The Panthers agreed a one-year contract with tight end Darren Waller, terms undisclosed; the 33-year-old caught 24 passes for 283 yards and six touchdowns in nine games for Miami last season. France's newly hired coach Zinedine Zidane appointed Fabien Barthez as goalkeeper coach, reuniting the World Cup-winning pair as Zidane builds his backroom staff.

Other developments: Celta Vigo's La Liga season opener against Osasuna was postponed from August 17 after a fungal outbreak made the pitch at Estadio de Balaidos unfit for play; La Liga rescheduled it for August 27, though Osasuna disputed the decision, saying both clubs had previously agreed to play during the international break in late September. Russell Westbrook announced his retirement after 18 NBA seasons, closing out a career as the league's all-time triple-double leader with 209, along with 27,176 points and 10,351 assists. Katie Ledecky won the 1,500-metre freestyle at the Pan Pacific Championships in 15:36.09, extending a winning streak in the event to 16 years, while a U.S. quartet set a mixed medley relay world record of 3:36.70. The Lakers' agreed sale to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger at $12.5 billion remains pending NBA board of governors approval in September.

CTE research advanced as a separate strand: as reported this morning, Matt Hasselbeck underwent scans and cognitive tests at Boston University as part of a multi-site study attempting to develop the first living diagnosis for chronic traumatic encephalopathy, funded by a $15 million National Institutes of Health award.
